vendors.name: Oracle Aconex
vendors.tagline: Oracle's cloud document control and project collaboration platform
vendors.market_position: Oracle Aconex is a cloud platform where the owner, consultants and contractors on a project share documents, formal correspondence (Mail) and review workflows in one record; Oracle announced its purchase of Aconex in December 2017. Oracle's Aconex status page lists a Middle East (MEA) instance and a separate Saudi Arabia (KSA1) instance. Construction Business News Middle East reported in January 2017 that Aconex was deployed for a Kuwait causeway project.
pros: Documents, Mail and approval workflows in one shared project record
Middle East (MEA) instance listed by Oracle
Oracle Aconex Mobile app for site teams
Still developed: Oracle announced new Aconex capabilities in April 2026
cons: No public prices: quote from Oracle
Built for multi-party projects, more than a small contractor needs
Not an accounting or invoicing tool
Support Central help is not offered in Arabic
vendors.kw_specific_note: Aconex suits clients, consultants and main contractors who need one shared record of documents and correspondence across many companies on a large project. Kuwait has no VAT in force (vatcalc.com reported in July 2026 that it is expected in 2028 or later), and Aconex does not handle invoicing, so accounts stay in a separate system.

vendors.name: Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud)
vendors.tagline: Autodesk's construction platform, now sold as Autodesk Forma
vendors.market_position: Autodesk moved Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC) into its Autodesk Forma brand on 24 March 2026 and renamed the products, for example Forma Build, Forma Data Management, Forma Takeoff and Forma Estimate. Autodesk sells them in three quote-based bundles, Model Management, Preconstruction and Construction Operations, which also include Navisworks Manage, BuildingConnected Pro, ProEst and Pype tools.
pros: Model coordination, design collaboration and document management in one account
Bundles run from takeoff, estimating and bidding to field operations and closeout
User-, project- and account-based pricing options (per Autodesk)
30-day money-back guarantee stated on the pricing page
cons: No public prices for the construction bundles: quote-based
Product names changed in March 2026, so older guides use ACC names
Not an accounting or invoicing tool
BIM depth is more than simple jobs need
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based: Autodesk's construction pricing page lists three bundles (Model Management, Preconstruction, Construction Operations) with 'Get a quote' and no prices; Autodesk says it offers user-, project- and account-based pricing and a 30-day money-back guarantee.
vendors.kw_specific_note: No Kuwait reseller or local office was confirmed in this check, so ask any Kuwait seller whether it is an authorised Autodesk partner and who provides local support and training. The tools suit engineering firms and contractors working with BIM models; simple jobs do not need them.

vendors.name: PlanRadar
vendors.tagline: Site inspections, snagging, defects and site documentation
vendors.market_position: PlanRadar, launched in Vienna in 2013, is a site documentation, inspection and defect-management app that says it has more than 200,000 users in 75+ countries. It has no Kuwait site or office; its nearest office is in Downtown Dubai, and it runs Arabic-language UAE and Saudi websites. It publishes per-user prices in USD, EUR, GBP and AUD, and subcontractors join free on every plan.
pros: Published per-user prices and a 30-day free trial
Unlimited subcontractors and watchers free on every plan
Arabic-language regional website and pricing page
PlanRadar says the platform runs in more than 18 languages
cons: Site execution only, not scheduling or accounting
Starter and Pro are capped at 10 users; more needs Enterprise
4% innovation fee on the annual fee from the second billing period
No Kuwait office and no prices in KWD
vendors.typical_pricing: Published (USD, per user per month): Basic $32 (1 user, 10 plans), Starter $107 (up to 10 users, 30 plans per user), Pro $159 (up to 10 users, 100 plans per user, 1 BIM model per user); Enterprise by quote. PlanRadar says annual billing saves more than 10%, bills annually in advance unless the contract says otherwise and adds a 4% innovation fee from the second billing period. 30-day free trial.
vendors.kw_specific_note: PlanRadar has no Kuwait office or Kuwait website; its nearest office is in Dubai, and prices are in USD rather than KWD. It suits contractors who want digital snagging, inspections and handover records without an enterprise rollout.

vendors.name: Focus Softnet
vendors.tagline: ERP, CRM and HR suite with construction project costing and CAFM
vendors.market_position: Focus Softnet, established in 1992 and headquartered in Hyderabad, India, sells the Focus X ERP with CRM, HCM, CAFM and real-estate modules and says it operates from 27 offices in 17 countries. It has a Kuwait office in Panasonic Tower on Fahad Al-Salem Street, Kuwait City. Its Kuwait construction ERP page covers project budgets and milestones, procurement, cost control, payroll and site updates.
pros: Kuwait City office with a local phone line
Construction ERP covers project budgets, procurement, cost control and payroll
Focus CAFM for facility management and maintenance work orders
Cloud or on-premise deployment; multilingual and multi-currency (per Focus)
cons: No public prices: brochure, demo and quote only
Broad suite, more than a small contractor needs
Arabic interface not stated on the Kuwait pages
ERP implementation effort
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices (brochure download and free demo).
vendors.kw_specific_note: Focus runs a Kuwait office in Kuwait City (Panasonic Tower, Al-Quibla area) and lists service areas including Hawally, Salmiya, Fahaheel and Shuwaikh. Its Kuwait pages do not name PIFSS or Kuwait Labour Law payroll rules, so ask for a demo of local payroll and Arabic screens before buying.

vendors.name: In4Suite (In4Velocity)
vendors.tagline: Real-estate and construction ERP from India, sold in the Gulf from Dubai
vendors.market_position: In4Velocity Systems, based in Bangalore, India, sells In4Suite, an ERP for real-estate developers, contractors and infrastructure firms that covers land banking, project budgets and engineering, sales, leasing, property management, finance and HR and payroll. It runs a Kuwait landing page but no Kuwait office; its Middle East office is in Business Bay, Dubai. In4Velocity says it has more than 700 clients in over 21 countries.
pros: Covers land, projects, sales, leasing and property management in one system
Construction project budgets and engineering module
HR and payroll included
Kuwait landing page and a Dubai office for the Gulf
cons: No public prices: demo and quote only
No Kuwait office; contact is a UAE number
Leans to property developers more than small trade contractors
Kuwait page names no Kuwait-specific features such as PIFSS payroll
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices (demo on request).
vendors.kw_specific_note: In4Velocity lists Kuwait among its markets but gives no Kuwait address; the Kuwait page's contact is a UAE phone number, and its Middle East office is in Dubai. It fits firms that develop and sell or lease property as well as build; ask how Kuwait payroll rules are handled before buying.

vendors.name: Matiyas Solutions
vendors.tagline: ERPNext implementer with Kuwait payroll and construction set-ups
vendors.market_position: Matiyas Solutions implements ERPNext, the open-source ERP; Frappe lists it as a Bronze Partner in India, and Matiyas lists offices in India, Nigeria and a Kuwait office in Munira Tower, Fahaheel. Its Kuwait page says its set-up handles Kuwait Labour Law payroll, PIFSS contributions for Kuwaiti nationals, WPS files, KWD and an Arabic right-to-left interface. Its construction ERP covers BOQ import, project budgets, subcontract billing with retention, and labour payroll.
pros: Kuwait payroll set-up: Labour Law, PIFSS and WPS (per Matiyas)
Construction features: BOQ import, budgets, subcontract billing and retention
Arabic right-to-left interface and KWD handling (per Matiyas)
Built on ERPNext, which is open source
cons: No public prices: demo and quote only
Kuwait page gives an Indian phone number
Results depend on the implementation partner, not a packaged product
ERPNext needs configuration before use
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices (demo on request).
vendors.kw_specific_note: Matiyas lists an office in Munira Tower, Mecca Street, Fahaheel, and says its ERPNext set-up covers Kuwait Labour Law payroll, PIFSS contributions and WPS files. Its Kuwait contact details are an Indian phone number and email, so ask who will support you locally.

vendors.name: Central Agency for Public Tenders (CAPT)
vendors.tagline: Kuwait's public tenders agency; classifies general contractors
vendors.market_position: The Central Agency for Public Tenders (CAPT) runs and approves Kuwait government tenders and contract awards, and its classification committee sorts general contractors into four categories by financial and technical capability. Arab Times reported in late September 2026 that Decree-Law No. 94 of 2026 amends the Public Tenders Law: once in force, three months after gazette publication, government entities may sign contracts up to KD 1 million without CAPT approval, and local or commission agents are banned from contracting procedures.
pros: Runs and approves large government tenders and contract awards
Classifies general contractors into four categories
Amended law gives SMEs priority when within 10% of the lowest acceptable bid
CAPT is to set special conditions to ease SME entry to the fourth category
cons: Rules change when Decree-Law No. 94 of 2026 takes effect, about three months after late-September 2026 gazette publication
Classification depends on proven financial and technical capability
CAPT's website did not load for this check, so fees and forms were not confirmed
Local and commission agents banned from contracting procedures under the amendment
vendors.typical_pricing: Government agency; no fees confirmed (CAPT's website could not be read for this check).
vendors.kw_specific_note: Under the amended Public Tenders Law, the classification committee sorts general contractors into four categories by financial and technical capability, and CAPT is to set easier entry conditions for SMEs in the fourth category. Keep financial statements and project records ready before applying, and check CAPT's current rules after Decree-Law No. 94 of 2026 takes effect.

vendors.name: Kuwait Tax (Ministry of Finance)
vendors.tagline: Kuwait's corporate income tax, 5% payment retention and Pillar Two top-up tax
vendors.market_position: Kuwait's Ministry of Finance, through its Department of Income Tax, administers corporate income tax at a flat 15% on foreign entities doing business in Kuwait and on GCC companies to the extent of their foreign ownership; companies wholly owned by Kuwaiti or other GCC nationals are exempt. Kuwait has not introduced VAT. Since 1 January 2025 a 15% Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax under Decree-Law No. 157 of 2024 applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more.
pros: No VAT in force in Kuwait
Companies wholly owned by Kuwaiti or GCC nationals are outside corporate income tax
No withholding tax on payments
No excise taxes
cons: 15% corporate income tax on foreign entities and on the foreign-owned share of GCC companies
Payers retain 5% of contract payments until a tax clearance certificate is shown
15% top-up tax for multinational groups with revenue of EUR 750 million or more
Kuwaiti shareholding companies pay 1% Zakat on net profits
vendors.typical_pricing: No service fee; the cost is the tax itself: 15% corporate income tax on the foreign-owned share of taxable profits, with 5% of contract payments retained until a tax clearance certificate is presented.
vendors.kw_specific_note: Kuwait has not introduced VAT, so VAT e-invoicing features sold for Saudi Arabia or the UAE do not apply here. For a contractor, the practical tax points are corporate income tax on any foreign ownership and the 5% retention clients hold back until you present a tax clearance certificate.

vendors.name: Public Authority for Manpower (Kuwaitization)
vendors.tagline: Kuwait's private-sector labour regulator: work permits, working hours and Kuwaitization
vendors.market_position: The Public Authority for Manpower (PAM) administers private-sector employment under Labour Law No. 6 of 2010, including work permits and their transfers. Since 1 November 2025 employers must record staff working schedules on a PAM electronic platform, and since 1 July 2025 non-Kuwaiti private-sector employees need an exit permit to leave the country. On government contracts, Cabinet Resolution No. 1179 of 2023 has each tendering body set the share of Kuwaiti workers per contract.
pros: One regulator for private-sector work permits and labour law
Working schedules and exit permits handled on electronic platforms
Work permits can be transferred after one year of service
cons: Government contracts carry Kuwaiti-hiring requirements set per contract
Violations can lead to suspension of the employer's file
Exit permit needed for every departure by non-Kuwaiti staff
Fees and sector quotas not readable online from outside Kuwait
vendors.typical_pricing: Government service fees; PAM's fee schedule could not be read on 2026-09-30 because its site was unreachable from outside Kuwait.
vendors.kw_specific_note: Contractors bidding for public work should expect Kuwaiti-hiring conditions: under Cabinet Resolution No. 1179 of 2023 each tendering body's Kuwaitisation Unit sets the proportion of Kuwaiti workers for the contract and can penalise non-compliance. Employer social security contributions go to a separate body, the Public Institution for Social Security (PIFSS).

vendors.name: Kuwait Municipality (Baladia)
vendors.tagline: Kuwait's authority for building permits and engineering-office licensing
vendors.market_position: Kuwait Municipality issues building permits and licenses engineering offices, and says both systems now run fully online. According to municipality figures reported in August 2026, private-housing building permits are issued in under 48 hours through the engineering-office system, and more than 85% of direct municipal services can be completed through Sahel, the government's unified services app.
pros: Building permits and engineering-office licensing handled online
Private-housing permits reported at under 48 hours
Most direct municipal services available through the Sahel app
Engineering plans held in a digitised building file
cons: Permit fees not readable online from outside Kuwait
In new residential areas, permits wait for the housing authority's certificate until infrastructure is complete
Inspectors record building violations and notify owners electronically
vendors.typical_pricing: Government permit fees; the Kuwait Municipality fee schedule could not be read on 2026-09-30 because its site was unreachable from outside Kuwait.
vendors.kw_specific_note: The municipality issues private-housing permits through its electronic engineering-office system and says most direct services can be completed in the Sahel app. Under an August 2026 Cabinet decision, plots in new residential areas cannot get the housing authority certificate needed for a permit until roads, power, water and sewage are finished, so check the area's status before quoting a build start.

vendors.name: Kuwait Fire Force (formerly KFSD)
vendors.tagline: Kuwait's fire authority: fire licences, sprinkler rules and inspections
vendors.market_position: The Kuwait Fire Force (KFF), known in earlier years as the Kuwait Fire Service Directorate (KFSD), licenses commercial and industrial premises for fire safety and inspects them. Since 2024 it requires sprinklers in all investment housing buildings, not only those over ten floors, and firefighting companies need its approval and must report to it monthly. Private homes are outside the fire law's mandatory requirements.
pros: Online check of any establishment's fire licence on kff.gov.kw
Clear rule: the building's licence comes before a tenant's
Approved firefighting companies report to KFF monthly
cons: Sprinklers required in every investment building regardless of height
Late licence renewal can bring fines or administrative closure
No fire licence for a rented unit in an unlicensed building
Licence fees not found on any page readable in this check
vendors.typical_pricing: Government licence fees; KFF's fee schedule could not be read on 2026-09-30 because kff.gov.kw blocked automated access.
vendors.kw_specific_note: For fit-out and MEP contractors, the fire licence is the gate: a shop or unit in a shared building, mall or commercial centre cannot be licensed unless the building holds a valid KFF licence, and investment buildings of any height now need sprinklers. Firefighting system installers need KFF approval.

vendors.name: Gulf Insurance Group (GIG Kuwait)
vendors.tagline: Fairfax-owned Kuwaiti composite insurer rated A+ by S&P
vendors.market_position: GIG-Kuwait (Gulf Insurance and Reinsurance Company) is the Kuwaiti composite insurer of Gulf Insurance Group, which was established in 1962 and is listed on Boursa Kuwait. Fairfax Financial Holdings has owned 97.06% of the group since a 2024 tender offer, and GIG says it has consistently led the Kuwaiti market by premiums written. S&P rates both the group and GIG-Kuwait A+ (August 2026), and AM Best affirmed both at A (Excellent) in September 2026.
pros: S&P A+ and AM Best A (Excellent) ratings for GIG-Kuwait itself, both stable
Owned 97.06% by Fairfax Financial Holdings
Composite insurer; the group has a separate takaful company for Sharia-compliant cover
cons: No public prices for commercial cover
Engineering and contractor products not visible on any page readable in this check
Conventional insurer; takaful cover sits in a separate company
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices found for commercial or contractor cover.
vendors.kw_specific_note: When a contract or lender requires a highly rated insurer, GIG-Kuwait's own ratings are S&P A+ (August 2026) and AM Best A (Excellent), affirmed in September 2026. Ask GIG directly for its contractors' all-risks and plant cover, as those products could not be checked online in this review.

vendors.name: Al Ahleia Insurance Company
vendors.tagline: Kuwaiti insurer since 1962 with a full engineering line, rated A by AM Best
vendors.market_position: Al Ahleia Insurance Company was established by Amiri Decree on 12 June 1962 and is listed on Boursa Kuwait. Its fire and general accident page lists contractors' all risks, erection all risks, contractors' plant and machinery, machinery breakdown and its loss of profit, electronic equipment and cold-store stock deterioration, plus public liability and workmen's compensation. Al Ahleia shows ratings of A (Excellent) from AM Best, A- with a positive outlook from S&P, and A3 with a positive outlook from Moody's.
pros: Contractors' all risks, erection all risks and plant and machinery cover listed by name
Workmen's compensation, employer's liability and public liability from the same insurer
Rated by three agencies: AM Best A, S&P A-, Moody's A3
Operating since 1962
cons: No public prices; engineering cover is quoted through the staff contacts on the product page
Conventional insurer; no takaful products shown on its product menu
Engineering products described on the website only in outline
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices on alahleia.com for engineering or liability cover.
vendors.kw_specific_note: For a Kuwaiti contractor, Al Ahleia's product page covers the whole project stack in one place: contractors' all risks or erection all risks for the works, plant and machinery cover for equipment, and workmen's compensation and public liability for staff and third parties.

vendors.name: First Takaful Insurance Company
vendors.tagline: Kuwaiti takaful insurer listing construction covers from CAR to decennial liability
vendors.market_position: First Takaful Insurance Company is a Sharia-compliant (takaful) insurer in Kuwait, listed on Boursa Kuwait, which says it introduced takaful insurance to the Kuwaiti market in 2000 as the first takaful operator. Its corporate page lists contractors' all risks, erection all risks, contractors' plant and equipment, machinery breakdown, boiler and pressure vessel, workmen's compensation, public liability and ten-year decennial liability. Moody's rates it Ba2 with a stable outlook (June 2026).
pros: Takaful (Sharia-compliant) cover with a Shari'a supervisory board
Construction covers listed by name, including decennial liability
Loss-of-profit cover after machinery breakdown
Workmen's compensation and public liability from the same insurer
cons: No public prices; quotes by request
Moody's rating Ba2, below investment grade
Only a Moody's rating is shown on its site; no S&P or AM Best rating listed
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices on firsttakaful.com.kw (quote request form).
vendors.kw_specific_note: First Takaful suits Kuwaiti contractors who want Sharia-compliant cover for the full project cycle, from contractors' all risks during works to decennial liability after handover. Its Moody's rating is Ba2, so check any employer or lender clause that sets a minimum insurer rating before relying on it as the sole insurer.

vendors.name: ProTenders
vendors.tagline: GCC construction project intelligence and eTendering, with Kuwait project coverage
vendors.market_position: ProTenders, launched in 2011 and run by Nuserv DMCC under UAE law, sells construction project intelligence and an eTendering tool across the six GCC states. Its Kuwait page says it tracks USD 194 billion of upcoming and ongoing Kuwaiti projects across planning, design, tender and construction stages, with participant details including decision-makers' emails and phone numbers. Companies can list a free profile and bid on private tenders; the intelligence database is a paid, custom-priced plan.
pros: Kuwait projects tracked from planning through construction
Participant details, including decision-makers' contacts, in the paid plan
Free company profile that can bid on private tenders
eTendering tool for running your own tenders
cons: Intelligence and eTendering plans are custom-priced, with no published figures
Project and contact data need sign-up and a paid plan
No Kuwait office; offices in Abu Dhabi and Montreal
Project totals on the Kuwait page are ProTenders' own figures
vendors.typical_pricing: Company Profiles free; Construction Intelligence and Construction eTendering are custom-priced after a demo, with no published figures.
vendors.kw_specific_note: ProTenders has a dedicated Kuwait project database (it says USD 194 billion of upcoming and ongoing projects) aimed at contractors and suppliers who want to reach developers, consultants and main contractors before contracts are awarded. The free profile is a low-cost way to be listed; ask for a Kuwait sample in the demo before paying.

vendors.name: BNC Network
vendors.tagline: Construction project-intelligence database covering the GCC, wider Middle East, Africa and South Asia
vendors.market_position: BNC Network is a privately held construction project-intelligence company headquartered in Sharjah, UAE, which says it has operated since 2004 and covers over 37,000 live projects in 72 countries across the Middle East, Africa and South Asia. It sells project profiles with status updates, values, bidder information and contacts for owners, consultants, contractors and subcontractors, and describes its core as a database of GCC projects. An event sponsor profile names Industry Networks as its parent.
pros: Project status, values and bidder information
Contacts for owners, consultants, contractors and subcontractors
Running since 2004 (BNC's statement)
GCC-wide project database, useful for firms bidding in several markets
cons: No public prices found
Site loads by script; little detail visible before contacting sales
No readable page lists Kuwaiti projects specifically
No Kuwait office named; headquarters in Sharjah
vendors.typical_pricing: No public prices found on bncnetwork.net.
vendors.kw_specific_note: BNC sells GCC-wide project data, which takes in Kuwait, but none of the pages readable in this check showed its Kuwaiti project coverage. Ask BNC for a sample of Kuwaiti projects in your sector before paying for a subscription.
